At :417-419 it splits seq_len(B) into actual_cores chunks; the policy is not forced serial for this class (globals.R:978-983). At 1 core it runs run_chunk() serially on the parent's set.seed(seed) stream (:426-427). At 2 cores it calls private$par_lapply(chunks, run_chunk, n_cores = 2) (:429). par_lapply (R/EDI/R/inference_all_abstract.R:985) takes the fork branch and calls parallel::clusterSetRNGStream(worker_cl, private$seed) (:1057, or :1112 for a lazy cluster), so each worker starts its own L'Ecuyer stream. The mirai branch instead seeds each chunk with seed_val + i (:1084-1086). Inside each worker, draw_one() calls private$bootstrap_sample_indices() (inference_proportion_gcomp.R:367), which calls Design$draw_bootstrap_indices() (design_abstract.R:1028-1029), which calls sample_int_replace_cpp(); that function seeds from R::unif_rand() (src/fast_sample_int.cpp:103). The resampled indices, and so the bootstrap distribution, change with set_num_cores().

set.seed(20261117)
	n = 50L
	X = data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
	y_base = stats::plogis(rnorm(n))
	on.exit(unset_num_cores(), add = TRUE)
	run = function(cores) {

		d$assign_w_to_all_subjects()

		inf = InferencePropGCompMeanDiff$new(d)
		inf$set_seed(3L)
		inf$approximate_bootstrap_distribution_beta_hat_T(B = 40L, show_progress = FALSE)
	}

	b2 = run(2L)

test_name: seeded g-computation proportion bootstrap distribution does not depend on the core count
text: Inference$par_lapply() gives FUN a different R random stream depending on the core count. In the serial branch (n_cores <= 1) it calls set.seed(private$seed), which gives a Mersenne-Twister stream. In the fork branches (persistent global cluster, the retry cluster, or the lazy cluster) it calls parallel::clusterSetRNGStream(worker_cl, private$seed), which gives every worker its own L'Ecuyer-CMRG stream. In the mirai branch it seeds each chunk with private$seed + i, and the number of chunks is 4 * n_cores. A FUN that draws random numbers therefore sees draws that depend on how the work is split across workers, not on the draw index. One public path that reaches this is InferencePropGCompMeanDiff$approximate_bootstrap_distribution_beta_hat_T(). It draws its bootstrap indices inside run_chunk via sample_int_replace_cpp(), which seeds from R::unif_rand(). With the same set_seed() it returns a different seeded bootstrap distribution at 1 core than at 2 cores. compute_reusable_bootstrap_worker_distribution() (non_param_boot.R:1499-1500) repeats the same per-chunk mirai seeding (private$seed + task$id, with chunk ids that depend on actual_cores).

child = function(cores) {
		suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(EDI))
		set_num_cores(cores)
		on.exit(unset_num_cores(), add = TRUE)
		n = 40L
		set.seed(20261117)
		X = data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
		yc = rpois(n, 3)
		d = DesignFixediBCRD$new(response_type = "count", n = n, seed = 7L, verbose = FALSE)
		d$add_all_subjects_to_experiment(X)
		d$assign_w_to_all_subjects()
		d$add_all_subject_responses(yc + d$get_w())
		inf = InferenceCountPoisson$new(d)
		inf$set_seed(3L)
		set.seed(1000L + cores)
		invisible(runif(7L * cores))
		t0 = inf$approximate_randomization_distribution_beta_hat_T(r = 200L, show_progress = FALSE)
		list(cores = EDI:::get_num_cores(), inf_cores = as.integer(inf$num_cores), t0 = as.numeric(t0))
	}
	run = function(cores) callr::r(
		child,
		args = list(cores = cores),
		env = c(callr::rcmd_safe_env(), NOT_CRAN = "true"),
		timeout = 280
	)
	r1 = run(1L)
	r2 = run(2L)
	expect_identical(r2$inf_cores, 2L)
	expect_identical(length(r1$t0), 200L)
	expect_identical(r1$t0, r2$t0)
test_name: seeded randomization distribution of a warm-started GLM is identical with 1 and 2 cores
text: The reused-worker randomization path splits the nsim permutations into chunk_n = num_cores contiguous chunks and, for concave likelihoods, chains the fit warm start from one permutation to the next within a chunk (base_fit_warm_start = previous converged params). With 1 core all permutations are one chain. With 2 cores the second chunk restarts from the full-data MLE (and its Fisher information) at permutation nsim/2+1. Each null fit therefore starts from a point that depends on the core count, so the optimizer stops at a slightly different iterate. The seeded randomization distribution (and anything cached from it) is not identical across core counts, even though the permutations are the same. For iterative fits with loose tolerances (L-BFGS Weibull, ordinal) the drift is larger than ulps.

text: compute_rand_bootstrap_two_sided_pval(type = "smoothed") builds its draws with materialize_w = FALSE, so no per-draw w_seed is recorded. The fresh assignment for each bootstrap draw is then drawn lazily inside the worker loop (des_obj$draw_ws_according_to_design) from whatever R RNG stream the executing process holds. With 1 core that is the parent's stream, seeded once by set.seed(private$seed). With 2 or more cores each fork or mirai worker has its own stream (clusterSetRNGStream / seed + chunk id). The assignments, the null distribution and the seeded p-value therefore change with set_num_cores() whenever the design itself is unseeded. The same lazy draw is taken on the default percentile path for classes whose supports_reusable_bootstrap_worker() is FALSE and that have no fast kernel (line 279 materializes only when has_fast_kernel || supports_reusable_bootstrap_worker()). Those draws go through par_lapply at line 378.

n = 200L
	set.seed(20261117)
	X = data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
	set.seed(99)
	W = lapply(1:6, function(b) { g = stats::rgamma(n, shape = 1, rate = 1); g / sum(g) * n })
	run = function(cores) {
		set_num_cores(cores)
		on.exit(unset_num_cores(), add = TRUE)
		d = DesignFixediBCRD$new(response_type = "count", n = n, seed = 7L, verbose = FALSE)
		d$add_all_subjects_to_experiment(X)
		d$assign_w_to_all_subjects()
		w = d$get_w()
		set.seed(123)
		zero = runif(n) < stats::plogis(-0.2 + 0.4 * w + 0.3 * X$x1)
		y = ifelse(zero, 0, 1 + stats::rnbinom(n, mu = exp(0.6 + 0.3 * w + 0.2 * X$x2), size = 2))
		d$add_all_subject_responses(y)
		inf = InferenceCountHurdleNegBin$new(d, model_formula = ~ x1 + x2)
		inf$compute_estimate()
		priv = inf$.__enclos_env__$private
		priv$current_bayesian_bootstrap_context = priv$build_bayesian_bootstrap_context()
		est = vapply(W, function(wt) as.numeric(inf$compute_estimate_with_bootstrap_weights(wt, estimate_only = TRUE))[1L], numeric(1))
		list(nc = as.integer(inf$num_cores), est = est)
	}
	r1 = run(1L)
	r2 = run(2L)
	expect_identical(r1$nc, 1L)
	expect_identical(r2$nc, 2L)
	expect_true(all(is.finite(r1$est)))
	expect_identical(r1$est, r2$est)
test_name: hurdle negbin bootstrap-weighted estimates do not depend on the core count
text: InferenceCountHurdleNegBin$compute_estimate_with_bootstrap_weights() fits glmmTMB with control = glmmTMBControl(parallel = self$num_cores). This sends the EDI core count to TMB's OpenMP likelihood. With n threads, glmmTMB's observation loop (PARALLEL_REGION) is split across n tapes and the partial negative log-likelihoods and gradients are summed in a thread-dependent order. nlminb then follows a slightly different path, so the reweighted beta_hat_T for one weight vector differs between set_num_cores(1) and set_num_cores(2). Every Bayesian and nonparametric bootstrap replicate of this class therefore depends on the core count, which breaks the bit-identical seeded-result contract checked in test-rand-seed-core-count-invariance-two-session.R.

text: fit_zero_augmented_model() passes glmmTMBControl(parallel = self$num_cores) to glmmTMB, so TMB evaluates the likelihood on self$num_cores OpenMP threads. The per-thread partial sums of the negative log-likelihood and gradient are combined in a thread-count-dependent order, so the fitted coefficients differ in the low bits between 1 and 2 cores. The bootstrap-weighted estimate of InferenceCountHurdlePoisson (and the other zero-augmented subclasses, plus their use_rcpp = FALSE fits) therefore changes with set_num_cores(), and so do the seeded bootstrap distributions built from it.
